verdicts.question: Is the cable routing in the site photos continuous and consistent across the documented run — from rooftop panels to DCDB to inverter to ACDB to solar meter to main panel — with no orphan ends, no unexplained mid-run size changes, and visible conduit / cable-tie / clipping where the run is exposed?
verdicts.designer_notes: No designer answer for this target -- the vision routine verifies it by tracing cables across photos with 'Cable Routing', 'Equipment Location', 'Meter Box' and similar captions on pages 4+.
verdicts.photo_observation: Using the Cable Routing Legend (p.4): a red (DC Cable) line runs from the roof array through a labeled 'Hole' (p.11 img1) down into the utility landing where it connects to DCDB, then to the Inverter and Battery (p.11 img2, red lines); a purple (AC Cable) line connects Inverter to ACDB (p.11 img2). Green earthing-cable lines run from the same hole along wall-mounted conduit pipes (p.12 img1) toward the DC/AC Earth Pit markers (p.14). An orange (LA Cable) line runs along ceiling conduit pipework (p.13 img1) toward the LA Pit marker (p.14). The Equipment Location photo (p.13 img2) shows a further purple line/markers between the Solar meter and Main meter boxes, continuing the AC path onward. No leg of the traced path terminates without connecting to the next labeled component, and conduit pipes are visibly clipped to the walls/ceiling throughout the exposed runs.
verdicts.rationale: The color-coded overlays consistently chain each cable type from origin to destination across pages 11-14 with visible conduit support and no orphan ends, though this reflects a proposed routing plan overlaid on a pre-installation (under-construction) site rather than as-built cabling, which limits confidence to medium.
